name: IceCube Collaboration
notes: Institution-level membership rows are owned by the membership-lead workstream and are not written here; only the published aggregate counts are recorded.

Leadership is left empty because person records are owned by another workstream. The February 2026 press release identifies “Erin O’Sullivan, IceCube Spokesperson and a professor of physics at Uppsala University”, and the IceCube timeline records that Christian Spiering took over as IceCube spokesperson at the 2005 AMANDA/IceCube merger.
Derived field collaboration.experiment_ids is deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).
The AMANDA Collaboration merged into this collaboration on 20 March 2005.

summary.plain: The international team that runs the IceCube telescope at the South Pole: about 450 scientists at 58 universities and laboratories in 14 countries. It grew out of the earlier AMANDA team in 1999.
summary.technical: International collaboration formed in 1999 with the first IceCube proposal (lead institution University of Wisconsin–Madison, which holds the NSF maintenance and operations grant); about 450 scientists at 58 institutions in 14 countries as of January 2025. Absorbed the AMANDA Collaboration on 20 March 2005.
